notes:
CRM notes (shorthand):
- Primary problem: search across decades of long-form media transcripts (30k-200k tokens per file after OCR). Users complain about noisy top-K and slow relevance.
- Scale: initial POC ~5M chunks (expected expansion to 50M+ chunks if dedupe/sharding goes well). Backend store currently Postgres + S3 for raw, planning vector index for embeddings.
- "Chunking strategy" discussed in-depth: semantic chunking preferred for long transcripts (scene boundaries + speaker turns) vs naive fixed 2k-token windows. Need overlap 128-256 tokens on semantic boundaries to preserve context for reranker. Evaluate two passes: coarse fixed chunking for fast recall (ANN) then semantic merge before reranking.
- "Reranker tuning" specifics: prefer cross-encoder on top-50 from ANN; target rerank latency <= 120-180ms (p50/p95) per query at 50 qps baseline. Looking at batching for GPU cross-encoder (batch size tradeoffs) and quantized models to control cost.
- Embeddings model: testing an open MPNet variant + candidate smaller dense model for cold-start. Concern: embedding dimensionality vs storage (50M vectors -> estimate storage + cost).
- Cost targets: aiming for $0.0025 - $0.01 per query depending on top-K and reranker slice. Need Redwood Optimize suggestions on batching + KV caching to meet these targets.
- Security & compliance: must support VPC/private deployment, KMS integration, and audit logs for all query traffic. EMEA residency requirement for legacy vault (subset ~20% of content).
- Quotes from lead search engineer: "We need results that respect narrative continuity — slicing by paragraph is killing recall on long scenes."
- Open technical questions: best practice for index sharding across metadata (date/source), memory/cost tradeoff for precomputed cross-encoder features, and rollback plan if reranker introduces hallucinations.
- Next step: ingest sample dataset (5k long files) by 2026-03-14; run baseline ANN + reranker runs; deliver cost/latency matrix and recommended config.
summary: Enterprise media archive (Epochal) evaluating Redwood for RAG search. Large long-doc archive, heavy emphasis on embeddings + reranking, tight latency and cost constraints. POC planned to measure index scale, per-query cost, and reranker tuning tradeoffs.
